hook_text: In a desert city five hundred years ago, the best-selling product wasn't gold. It was books.
clip_script: Timbuktu, in the 1500s. Caravans bring salt and cloth, but the traveller Leo Africanus noticed something else: handwritten books earned more profit than any other goods. The city had more than a hundred and fifty schools. Students crossed the desert to study with famous masters at mosques like Sankore. They studied law, but also maths for trade, astronomy to calculate prayer times and the calendar, medicine, history and geography. When a master was satisfied, he gave a certificate: you may now teach this book. The greatest scholar, Ahmad Baba, owned about sixteen hundred books, and said his library was one of the smallest in his family. So next time someone says Africa had no written history, tell them about Timbuktu.
visual_style: A whiteboard market with a scale weighing gold against a stack of books, the books winning; students on wooden boards; a star chart; a scholar surrounded by shelves of manuscripts.
pacing: Twist hook, a tour of the subjects, a powerful closing line.
